name: InstaBox
oneLiner: Firecracker machines with a browser desktop, sold as a subscription that is also a monthly credit.
whatItIs: InstaBox sells full Linux virtual machines, one per AI agent, that boot in about a second, keep their disk between sessions, and can be paused with memory and running processes intact.

Each machine is a Firecracker microVM running Debian 13 with its own kernel, root, systemd and Docker, with NVIDIA L4 GPU machines on paid plans. You drive it from a web dashboard, a CLI, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a hosted MCP server or plain HTTP, and you can watch or take over its graphical desktop.

The intended buyer is a team running coding or computer-use agents that needs a real machine per task, not a single shared dev box. InstaBox is not InstaCloud, InsForge's separate managed-backend product.
whoFor: Teams and individuals running agents that need a persistent, general-purpose Linux box with a browser and desktop, who are comfortable with a CLI or API.
isolation: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel, root and passwordless sudo. Docker works. Templates are versioned images; you cannot bring your own OCI image.
sizes: Fixed vCPU/RAM pairs by plan: Free is 4/8 only; Pro adds 2/4 and 8/16; Builder goes to 16/32; Team to 32/64. GPU machines carry 1–4 NVIDIA L4s (11 vCPU / 36 GiB each) on paid plans. One disk at `/data`, 20 GiB by default, growable live to 200 GiB on Pro and 1,024 GiB on Team.

billing.model: Monthly subscription that is also a credit: $20, $100 or $500, reset monthly.
billing.meter: Per second while running, on the size you asked for: $0.004 per vCPU-hour, $0.00225 per GiB-hour, $0.00011 per GiB-hour for disk beyond the plan's included pool, $0.02 per GiB of egress beyond the allowance. NVIDIA L4 GPUs are $0.80 per GPU-hour on top.
billing.stopped: Disk only. Paid plans include 200 GiB (Pro), 1 TiB (Builder) or 5 TiB (Team) of disk across machines; snapshots and a paused machine's saved memory are free.
billing.planFee: The plan fee is the credit. Usage comes out of it first, then pay-as-you-go, and unused credit expires at month end.
billing.minimum: $20 a month on Pro, or the free plan: one 4/8 machine, five snapshots, 100 GiB of egress a month and runs of at most 480 minutes.

well: A real free plan: one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine that never converts and needs no card.
A browser desktop and a dashboard that creates the machine without a terminal.
Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode in the default image, with logins that persist in /data/home.
badly: An always-on agent on the free plan, which always pauses at 30 idle minutes.
A client-facing service on your own address: there is no custom domain.
EU data residency or a choice of region: machines run in the United States only.

usability.dashboard: Yes, a full console: create a machine from a template with a button, start/stop/pause, open the Computer tab to click the Linux desktop, publish ports, save snapshots from the Playground, read metrics and billing.
usability.withoutCode: Partly. Creating a machine, opening its desktop, using Chromium, publishing a port and saving a snapshot are all click-driven. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are preinstalled, so you can type a plain-English request into the box's terminal, or prompt an agent with `instabox agent prompt`. There is no hosted agent product and no prompt-in, result-out API.
usability.signup: GitHub or Google. Whether a brand-new free account needs a card is not published: the pricing page says $0, while the API has a `cardMissingAt` state that blocks free machines. Paid plans subscribe by card in the dashboard.
usability.docs: Documentation rebuilt on 6 November 2026, each page available as Markdown, plus an `llms-full.txt` bundle and a docs MCP server; pages state limits and failure modes. Support is email on paid plans, priority on Team, and there is a Discord. A public status page is at instabox.instatus.com.
tripsUp: The quick start is a terminal command, `npx instabox@latest sh`.
Two different off switches: pause keeps the session, stop does not, and you cannot stop a paused machine.
A snapshot does not save the session, only files and installs.
A fork copies files in seconds but not running programs, despite the homepage.
The free machine is not a server: it pauses after 30 idle minutes and runs at most 480 minutes at a time.
Public port URLs have no password; use a private port for a token.

caveats.issue: The homepage says a fork copies running processes; the docs say otherwise
caveats.detail: Marketing says fork a machine mid-run and lists Running Processes. The docs say a fork is a copy-on-write copy of the disks, and memory and running programs are not copied. This guide follows the docs.

evidence.quote: Memory and running programs are not copied

caveats.issue: Whether the free plan needs a card
caveats.detail: The pricing page says $0 and Get started; the API has a card-missing state that makes free sandboxes answer 402. It may apply only to workspaces that once had a paid plan.
Home is `/data/home`, so saved GitHub, Claude, Codex, git and SSH logins travel into every machine built from a snapshot.
A region field in a create request is refused; the Terms say data is stored and processed in the United States.

caveats.issue: Free runs are capped at 480 minutes
caveats.detail: The 19 October pricing post says the free machine has no usage limit; the current limits and auto-pause pages cap a free run at 480 minutes. This guide follows the current docs.

evidence.quote: machines run at most 480 minutes at a time

strengths: A dashboard that creates a machine and opens a clickable Linux desktop.
Pause that keeps memory and running programs, with paid plans including 200 GiB to 5 TiB of disk.
Org Secrets in proxy mode: the machine holds a placeholder, not the key.
Cheap per-hour rates: $0.004 per vCPU-hour and $0.00225 per GiB-hour.
Every surface: TypeScript and Python SDKs, a hosted MCP server, real SSH and NVIDIA L4 GPUs.
